front_blocks.md: Define the term **xylem**.

back_blocks.md: Xylem are vessels that **transport water **and** mineral ions **from the roots to the upper parts of plants.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Xylem vessels provide structural support to plant stems.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Xylem vessels are **strong** to enable them to transport water without breaking; this means that they also contribute to** structural support** within plant stems.

front_blocks.md: What is the role of a** root hair cell**?

back_blocks.md: The role of a root hair cell is to absorb **water** and **mineral ions** from the soil.

- They have a** large surface area**
- They contain mitochondria which release **energy** for **active transport**

front_blocks.md: Write a flow diagram to describe the **pathway taken by water** as it travels across the root, up the stem, and out of the leaves of plants.

back_blocks.md: The pathway taken by water as it travels across the root, up the stem, and out of the leaves of plants is:
**Root hair cells **$\rightarrow$**root cortex **$\rightarrow$**xylem vessels **$\rightarrow$** spongy mesophyll cells**

front_blocks.md: Define the term **transpiration**.

back_blocks.md: Transpiration is the **loss of water vapour** from the leaves of plants by **evaporation**.

cards.front_md: Define the term **transpiration**.
cards.back_md: Transpiration is the **loss of water vapour** from the leaves of plants by **evaporation**.

front_blocks.md: What is the role of the **spongy mesophyll cells** in transpiration?

back_blocks.md: The spongy mesophyll cells are involved in transpiration as follows:

- water vapour **evaporates** from the surface of spongy mesophyll cells and enters the leaf **air spaces**
- water vapour **diffuses** from the air spaces out of the leaf

back_blocks.md: Water vapour exits the leaf air spaces by the process of **diffusion** through the **stomata**.

front_blocks.md: Name the piece of equipment used to **measure transpiration rate** in a plant shoot.

back_blocks.md: The  piece of equipment used to measure transpiration rate in a plant shoot is known as a **potometer**.

cards.front_md: Name the piece of equipment used to **measure transpiration rate** in a plant shoot.

front_blocks.md: Describe how a **bubble potometer** works to measure transpiration rate.

back_blocks.md: A bubble potometer works to measure transpiration rate as follows:

- a **bubble** is introduced into a tube containing a cut plant stem
- as the plant transpires water is pulled up the stem, causing the **bubble to move**
- the **distance the bubble moves** in a **given time** indicates the transpiration rate

front_blocks.md: How can a potometer be set up to ensure that the system is **airtight**?

back_blocks.md: An airtight potometer system can be ensured as follows:

- a potometer can be **set up underwater** to prevent entry of air bubbles
- **petroleum jelly** can be used to seal any joins

front_blocks.md: How does the structure of the **spongy mesophyll layer** aid transpiration? (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: The structure of the spongy mesophyll layer aids transpiration as follows:

- the spongy mesophyll layer contains **air spaces** where the surface of spongy mesophyll cells come into contact with the air
- there is a** large internal surface area **where this cell-air contact occurs
- the large surface area** increases the rate at which water vapour evaporates** from the surface of spongy mesophyll cells

front_blocks.md: What is the relationship between **number of stomata **and **transpiration rate**? (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: The relationship between number of stomata and transpiration rate is as follows:
- the **more stomata**, the **faster the rate of transpiration** (and vice versa)

front_blocks.md: Define the term **transpiration pull**. (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: **Transpiration pull** occurs when **water** **is drawn up the xylem** to replace the water that is lost from the surface of spongy mesophyll cells by **evaporation**.

front_blocks.md: How do **forces of attraction** between water molecules enable** **transpiration pull? (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: Forces of attraction between water molecules enables transpiration pull because:

- each water molecule **pulls on the water molecule below**
- the water molecules move upwards in a **continuous column**

Transpiration rate increases at higher temperatures due to the increased **kinetic energy** of molecules. (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: **True.**
At higher temperatures water molecules have **more kinetic energy **and are more likely to **diffuse **out via the stomata.

front_blocks.md: Why does transpiration occur **faster** on a **windy day**? (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: Transpiration is faster on a windy day because wind **blows water vapour away** from the surface of leaves, **maintaining a water vapour concentration gradient** between the inside and the outside of leaves.

front_blocks.md: Why do plants **wilt**? (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: Plants wilt when they** lose water** and **cannot replace it **with water from the soil. The water loss causes the plant cells to lose their rigid structure and the **cell walls no longer provide support **to the plant.

Sources and sinks can be found in different parts of plants at different times of year. (**Extended Tier Only**)

front_blocks.md: Why does **phloem transport** not always occur in the same direction? (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: Phloem transport occurs in different directions depending on the time of year:

- During** early spring** sucrose will be transported **upwards**, from storage organs in the roots towards growing leaves and flowers
- During **summer **sucrose will be transported **downwards**, from photosynthesising leaves towards storage organs in the roots
